A place with a past

More than a structure.
A living legacy.

Nahrikhera Fort is a heritage property associated with the Naruka family, situated near Phagi in the Jaipur region of Rajasthan. Its weathered walls, arched entrance and traditional masonry connect the estate to the architectural character of the region.

Family-provided accounts identify Shri Bharat Singh Ji as the founder of the lineage associated with the fort. Today, the story is preserved through family memory, photographs and a continuing commitment to heritage.

Historical note
The supplied catalogue uses an older estimate of nearly 700 years. The current family estimate shared for this website is 500+ years. Exact founding dates and independent archival confirmation have not been established here, so the site avoids presenting an exact century as proven fact.

Lineage & legacy.

Family relationships shown from the supplied family catalogue and details shared for this project.

The family tree is presented as a living record, not as a substitute for formal genealogical documents. The known modern family line is shown clearly below; earlier generations can be expanded as verified records become available.

Founder in family tradition Bharat Singh Ji Beginning of the Nahrikhera heritage record
Last Jagirdaar · as recorded Govind Singh Ji Historical rulership and modern custodianship are distinct
Present custodian Dayal Singh Ji Family heritage stewardship
Next generation Mahaveer Singh Ji Son of Dayal Singh Ji
Family member Yash Vardhan Singh Naruka Son of Mahaveer Singh Ji
Family member Shaurya Vardhan Singh Naruka Son of Mahaveer Singh Ji

The catalogue also names Bajrang Singh Ji and Sawai Singh Ji in the lineage. Their exact links between the earlier and later generations should be checked against the original family tree before a more detailed branch diagram is published. Durga Kanwer and Santosh Kanwer are also recorded in the supplied family information as spouses of Dayal Singh Ji and Mahaveer Singh Ji respectively.
